notes.title: Kingmakers Dev Blog #3: Picking a Fight with History
notes.content:
[p]Greetings Kingmakers,[/p][p][/p][p]Welcome back to another Dev Blog, where we'll be going over Kingmakers' lore and the real life historical events that inspired our time travelling medieval sandbox. Let's dive right in![/p][p][/p][h2][b]Real Life History of the Welsh Rebellion[/b][/h2][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44889766/88e795fcfadbcddab6d7ac38cfc58a47500c215f.png"][/img][/p][p][i]Image: The Modern Universal British Traveller. c.1779[/i][/p][p][/p][p]After a failed rebellion in 1283, King Edward I of England conquered Wales, ending native independence and turning the country into an English vassal. To further establish control, the English King gave his son the title “Prince of Wales” and from then on, the title was designated for heirs to the English throne.

Fast forward to 1399, English King Richard II was usurped and killed by his cousin Henry IV. For Welsh nobles, especially Richard’s ally, Owain Glyndŵr, this was a devastating event. Henry IV supported his own English lords but ignored Welsh petitions, allowing his lords to abuse their power over the Welsh gentry. This injustice and resentment, combined with harsh new laws, ignited the start of Owain Glyndŵr’s revolt against English rule.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44889766/e6f13ed8dc4af0fae48ec111fcda1ff1005ec27f.jpg"][/img][i]Owain Glyndŵr. Image: Copyright Meinir Mathias[/i]
[/p][p]In 1400, the Welsh people proclaimed Owain Glyndŵr to be the Prince of Wales, launching a rebellion against the English that would last 15 years. Starting with just a few hundred men, he raided English settlements across north-east Wales. Initially, he was dismissed as a minor nuisance. However, despite being outnumbered, Glyndŵr defeated a much larger English army and renewed Welsh hopes and prophecies of independence.
[/p][p]Owain Glyndŵr’s superior knowledge of the Welsh landscape and growing local support made guerrilla warfare very effective, and by 1402 he achieved great victories. He even gained powerful allies, including the French, who sent troops and supplies. The rebellion spread across Wales, reaching its peak in 1404, when his people officially crowned Glyndŵr as Prince of Wales in a grand ceremony.
[/p][p]But the tide eventually turned. The English King Henry IV adapted his strategy and deployed superior resources. The constant battles drained Welsh resources, and some nobles even switched allegiance back to the English. Gradually, the loss of major strongholds and allies forced Owain Glyndŵr into hiding, and English control of Wales was restored.
[/p][p]Glyndŵr never accepted pardon and chose exile and defiance over submission. He vanished from history, where some say he died in 1415, others whisper he continued to live in hiding.[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44889766/f18c90cb39bec2a5837ae84457579a16ae0b7766.png"][/img] [i]Owain Glyndŵr from his great seal[/i][/p][p][/p][p]Owain Glyndŵr never fulfilled the prophecy, but his rebellion carved his name into legend. Wales remained under English rule, and history was written.
[/p][p]But what if ...?[/p][h2]
[b]In Kingmaker’s Lore[/b][/h2][p][/p][p]In Kingmakers’ [b][i]original [/i][/b]timeline, Owain Glyndŵr’s rebellion was victorious. He and his allies managed to conquer all of England, which set the world on a path toward technological superiority. [/p][p][/p][p]However, a malevolent, otherworldly force changed this original timeline, causing Wales to fail in its conquest of England. This is the history you and I are familiar with today. Unfortunately this altered timeline has led us to the present day, where petty squabbles between nations has stunted our development ... leaving us ripe for otherworldly conquest. [/p][p][/p][p]Now, to save the future, someone must return to the source where everything went wrong. And that someone is you.[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44889766/bebbea6f56dde9e4b6eeab872fd4d49702513d9f.png"][/img][/p][p]As an American mercenary, you are sent back to the 15th century to aid Glyndŵr’s rebellion and restore the original timeline. Armed with modern weapons and vehicles, you will take the lead to rebuild and command his troops, in hopes of turning the inevitable loss into victories.
[/p][p]Every fight and every siege is a chance to reshape history and secure a future worth living in, and give last true Prince of Wales the victory he never had.[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44889766/eec5f4c5706bfed86542fef35f546c17470df426.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][i] - The Kingmakers Team[/i][/p]

notes.title: Dev Blog #2: Bringing A Gun To A Sword Fight
notes.content:
[p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44889766/b529491a639941847509158db17297fa3c087c37.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Greetings time travelling merc,[/p][p]Welcome back to another dev blog! This time we’re delving into your modern arsenal and the vehicles you’ll get to wreak havoc with in Kingmakers. With only about seven weeks to go before Early Access release, things are getting heated, but we can’t wait to know which weapons make you feel like an unstoppable force from the future.[/p][p][/p][p]Kingmakers started with a simple question that many of us have dreamed of in a game: "What would happen if you brought modern weapons into a medieval battlefield?" Could a single person with a modern arsenal obliterate a medieval army? That idea alone unlocked a ton of gameplay possibilities. But when you introduce guns and explosives into large-scale medieval battles with thousands of soldiers, the balance of things gets technically complex. And that’s the challenge our passionate dev team has been excited to tackle.  [/p][p][/p][p][/p][h2][b]Real-Life Research and Armor Penetration[/b][/h2][p][/p][p]Just down the road from the office, we have a shooting range where we do hands-on testing and research. We fired various guns, from 9mm, .40, and even a .50 cal. We’ve also looked into how armor holds up against different types of ammo. In movies, you’ll often see arrows punch through steel plate, which is unrealistic, so in Kingmakers, a bow won’t get through a full plate of armor. We want the game to feel like a simulated medieval battlefield, so the balance between medieval armor against modern bullets is something we’ve been exploring a ton, which we touched on in our [b][url="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2109770/view/516342955916658766"]first dev blog[/url][/b] when we talked about troops and their three tiers of armor from steel, hardened steel, and gold titanium alloy.[/p][p][/p][p]With that said, we want the guns to feel realistic too. So a 9mm handgun, for example, can go through wooden shields and steel armor, but to hit through hardened steel, you will need something stronger, like the .50 cal Desert Eagle.[/p][p][/p][p]While we can’t use real-world trademarks in the game, we’ve modeled the weapons to closely resemble their real-life counterparts, so for the purpose of this dev blog only, we might refer to some of them in here by those familiar names.[/p][p]
[/p][h2][b]Weaponry[/b][/h2][p][/p][p]There’s a pretty big arsenal in Kingmakers, so we won’t list everything here, and part of the fun will be discovering it yourself when you play. But to give you an idea of some, you’ll have handguns like 9mm pistols, the .50 cal Desert Eagle, to 500 cal Magnums. On the rifle side, you’ll find AR-15s and AK-47s, to LMGs and non-automatic rifles like the BMG. Plus a range of submachine guns, shotguns, a minigun, stun gun to capture prisoners, a futuristic plasma gun, a grenade launcher, plenty of throwables and explosives, including calling down land mines, an airstrike, and a rocket turret. And finally, bows, crossbows, and the sledgehammer for melee that you’ll always have with you.[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44889766/6c501389daf16cc32109e46159b5ab0209d9b89b.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44889766/a2e28796da41dfd2e49f58bfab0b1b888c68d47b.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44889766/b01bc878561ea39119a8ae2b5662d984bf2f71df.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][h2][b]Melee and Bows[/b][/h2][p][/p][p]When it comes to melee, we originally had a sword and shield for you, but realistically, swinging a sword at full plate armor isn’t very effective; that’s why we swapped it with the big sledgehammer. It's heavy, blunt impact is much more practical, and can help you stagger the tougher officers you’ll face. You’ll still have a shield, but it’s a small buckler that stays on your arm while you handle a gun, letting you parry incoming attacks or arrows without being weighed down like a heater or kite shield would. As for the bow and crossbow, you’ll be given modern versions, such as a rapid-fire crossbow and a semi-automatic bow that reloads like a modern firearm.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44889766/57931394fffe2a7e1c4d33cb624fd13ca6ff0f91.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][h2][b]Progression and Upgrades[/b][/h2][p][/p][p]When you start a mission, you’ll begin with lower tier weapons, like the bow, crossbow, or a basic handgun and a couple of grenades, and gradually unlock more powerful options as you progress.
[/p][p]In Kingmakers’ lore, the future is in rough shape and suffering from low resources, so requesting new guns isn’t that simple. You’ll need to loot in the past, gather resources like copper, gold, and hidden treasures, and send them back to the future. This will be your form of currency to buy new weapons and upgrades.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44889766/7a6ea0c8ee711a92dd897b6a85427d265eb2f23e.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Upgrades make a real difference in gameplay. You can improve things like a weapon’s magazine capacity, its armor pen, or its accuracy at range. A basic version of a weapon may start weak against the high-tier armors, but fully upgrading it could allow it to match those elite opponents.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44889766/e21cbb2150da21edc29b39fab472d13cf3888795.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][h2][b]Vehicles[/b][/h2][p][/p][p]At Early Access launch, there will be three player driveable vehicles available: a motorcycle, a convertible car, and we’re [i]hoping[/i] to get the tank in on time too. We went with the convertible over the pickup truck from the announcement trailer because it lets you shoot in 360 degrees (and look awesome while doing so). Whereas a closed roof would have limited you to fixed positions. That said, we’re not ruling the truck out completely. Early Access is all about feedback, so if the community wants it, then we will bring it back.[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44889766/b5bbe8405d971779df76e97602ed387d74635e55.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]In co-op, you won’t be able to share vehicles with teammates yet; instead, you will each have your own. But that’s something we’re hoping to add later in post-Early Access.
[/p][p]For gameplay reasons, the motorcycle is indestructible for now, but the convertible isn’t, so smashing through soldiers or obstacles will damage the car, and it can eventually be destroyed.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44889766/a82a64c8ffd12ac0ade169e03b09cc0551e6e1ef.gif"][/img][/p][p]
And a little fun fact about the vehicles: you can pull off some cool stunts, like launching off hills or crashing into buildings to mow down enemies. We hope you’ll share your daredevil gameplay clips with us if you do![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44889766/b740bb2a8c6f501c3046b1db28ba7050e2d531cf.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][h2][b]Destruction and Physics[/b][/h2][p][/p][p]Every weapon in Kingmakers has a penetration rating and interacts with the destructible environment differently, whether it’s plaster, wood, or stone. High-caliber guns, like LMGs such as the Norma, can shoot through multiple walls and even take out several soldiers behind it with a single shot. 
[/p][p]When it comes to destroying buildings, explosives, sledgehammers, and certain renown abilities will do the trick fast. Grenades and other explosives damage everything in their blast radius, regardless of armor, though the effect on enemies depends on their size and armor tier. Elite officers might stagger from an explosion, but regular soldiers will go flying or even have their body blow apart entirely.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44889766/057ff7bbc7388f2cc66dfbbb0b0866a89793052b.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44889766/efd95e55585a15115b01c0766dcd4112306a159e.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][h2][b]Future Plans and Unique Weapons[/b][/h2][p][/p][p]Looking ahead, we’ll be working on adding some more unique weapons and features post Early Access launch. One of the bigger additions we’re excited about is a helicopter for you to pilot. We’re also exploring flamethrowers and incendiary bombs, which will allow you to set large areas on fire. And there’s a drone currently in the works that will follow you around, but it likely won’t make it in time for Early Access.
[/p][p]Thanks so much for checking out our deep dive into weapons and vehicles in Kingmakers! We hope this gives you a better idea of what’s waiting for you when [b]Early Access drops on October 8th[/b]. We can’t wait to see how you experiment with your modern arsenal. Leave us a comment to let us know which weapons you’re most excited about![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44889766/fe6071ecdac4963cb1a211cf5c2c37f6ef8724ff.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Stay tuned for the next dev blog, and don’t forget to [b][url="https://discord.gg/fTvDsAYDfU"]join the Discord[/url][/b] to tell us what you want to see covered next![/p][p][/p][list][*][p][i]The Kingmakers Team[/i][/p][/*][/list][p]
[dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/2109770/Kingmakers/"][/dynamiclink][/p]

notes.title: Dev Blog #1: Meet the Troops You'll Command in Kingmakers
notes.content:
[p]Welcome to the first Kingmakers Dev Blog, a behind-the-scenes look at some of the amazing work the dev team at Redemption Road Games has been up to.[/p][p]For our first blog, we’re kicking things off with the allies you’ll be in command of - your units. Diving into the top-down strategy gameplay of Kingmakers massive medieval battlefield. So buckle up and let’s begin![/p][p][/p][h2][b]Unit Types[/b][/h2][p][/p][p]When Early Access hits, you'll have six medieval troop types to recruit, which include: Swordsmen, Spearmen, Cavalry, Archers, Berserkers, and Men-at-arms. Most of which will be upgradeable up to two or three tiers to improve their proficiency. For example; regular Archers can be upgraded to Longbowmen who cause extra armor-ruining ranged damage. There’s also a full skill tree system that enhances units even further, but more on that later.[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44889766/f1d52103d4f4b0de94321f6fc9d3fc607612f617.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Troops are just the beginning.
You’ll also have access to siege weapons like Trebuchets, Ballistas and the Archer Towers to place strategically. And let’s not forget, you’re a time-traveling mercenary. That means you can call in modern emplacements, such as gatling turrets, by tossing tactical grenades that drop them directly onto the battlefield, shredding medieval armor. However, keep note these turrets aren’t invincible, enemies can destroy them and they’re treated as deployable units, so place smart.[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44889766/9b2745c0852f50a66eb827973734760baebb3043.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][h2][b]Unit Strengths, Weaknesses, and Battlefield Roles[/b][/h2][p][/p][p]Every troop in Kingmakers have unique roles, bringing their own strength, weaknesses and behaviors on the battlefield. Think of it like rock-paper-scissors, if the scissors were a bow and arrow, and the rock rode a horse. Let’s break it down:[/p][list][*][p][b]Swordsmen[/b] gain defensive bonuses when positioned near other units, especially Archers.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Spearmen[/b] are effective against Cavalry. They can slow or knock riders off horses on impact.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Cavalry[/b] are fast and brutal, great for smashing through lines or flanking to reach Archers.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Archers[/b] are powerful against lightly armored units like Spearmen and Axemen but vulnerable to melee troops.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Berserkers [/b]wield axes and can enter a rage mode to deal high burst damage.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Men-at-arms [/b]are heavily armored macemen and act as the tanks. They can temporarily boost their defense to hold the line in heavy assaults.[/p][/*][/list][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44889766/0a5af6af7272815ceeb422085adfd63274e241c1.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Since you’re sided with the underdogs, you’ll be outnumbered and need to plan ahead. That means mixing and matching your troops and getting them into position before facing the enemy. Some examples of our personal favorite combos are; massed Archers protected by Swordsmen, great for efficiently leveling a village or outpost. Cavalry charges are also really satisfying to watch overwhelm and scatter your enemy. We also like combining Macemen and Axemen for a tight flanking wedge or crushing from the sides in a pincer move. But that’s just a couple examples of possibilities. We’re excited to see what kind of army combination [i]you[/i]’ll be creating.[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44889766/6b038875120a577b2e73e77af4424089fc49f736.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][h2][b]Unit Upgrades and Survival[/b][/h2][p][/p][p]Circling back to the skill tree, you can upgrade units through the skill tree by using holy relics collected during gameplay. The skill tree isn’t tied to individual units, it includes branches that enhance various troop types and unlock new abilities, like the Berserkers going into rage mode or the Men-at-arms getting extra tanky with a defense boost.[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44889766/223682278bea5d3dc1f5c52efdfb5e3961a9b6e4.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]As for keeping your army alive, you can throw tactical grenades that can heal units mid-fight, but in order to bring back those defeated, you’ll need to place down a hospital and bring the remaining survivors to it. Hospitals can revive fallen members and restore the full squad, so long as they’re only partially wiped out, if the entire troop is gone, then you’ll need to recruit a new one.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]Command and Control[/b][/h2][p][/p][p]Total War was a big inspiration for some of Kingmakers[i]’[/i] battlefield systems, but where their units behave as a single blob, our units are fully individual and AI-driven, more like what you’d see in Mount & Blade.[/p][p]In Kingmakers, you can seamlessly switch between top-down strategy and third-person combat at any time. In top-down, you’ll have full RTS-style control like in Total War or StarCraft in bird’s-eye view and a deep range camera zooming. We’re also exploring the idea of third-person commanding, where you’d run with an "honor guard" that follows your lead, but it won’t be in for Early Access.[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44889766/ed6ff548dba9260cc56cfc5c687854f059aa2e39.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][h2][b]Morale, Fear, and Prisoners[/b][/h2][p][/p][p]Enemy troops will have their own officers. When taking down an enemy officer, that troop’s morale will drop significantly, sometimes forcing a full-on retreat. There’s also a localized fear system; if enemies witness you blowing up another soldier, they might panic and flee.[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44889766/7142690ce5798b3c6a88708bbef165f1cb53526f.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]You can also capture officers using taser-based weapons to take them alive back to your prison and decide their fate. While you cannot convert enemy officers into an ally, you can choose to either ransom them for money, torture them for more resources or execute them for permanent morale boosts for your troops.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44889766/7bfb3962c0cfe873f85f0f6b4c8e987c8046cfd0.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44889766/d9bb75059b6fcea1a1249bd761ea7f6b348eecec.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Your own troops won’t have an officer because that role falls on you. And with that, you can unlock abilities that boost allied morale, either by staying close or tossing down support grenades. [/p][p][/p][p]Now, we’ve seen your questions as to how do these medieval troops feel about witnessing a gun-wielding demon from the future. And we’d love to add reactions like soldiers screaming “It’s a demon!”. But right now, it’s a stretch goal for post–Early Access. For now, the fear system already brings that immersive behavior on the battlefield.[/p][p][/p][p]You’ll also notice civilians such as peasants and nobles roam your growing stronghold and while they’re not part of any troop under your command, they do react when getting attacked. If confronted by enemy troops, they’ll either run and take cover in buildings or try to fight back, which will more likely end poorly as they are very weak. On that note, noblemen can also appear in missions where you can escort them or raid their convoys.[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44889766/6adc30b3e6241fef857d57c391b09cdb95c80fb1.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][h2][b]Enemy Officers and Armors[/b][/h2][p][/p][p]About those enemy officers we mentioned, there’s a lot more than one type and some don’t mess around, no matter how intimidating you are. Each comes with their own troop and fighting style. For example, the Shielded Pikemen march forward with their shields raised and throw spears at you, while the Warhammer brutes hit wide areas with big swings. There are even suicide bombers to watch out for, but we won’t spoil everything just yet and let you find out the fun way when you meet them ingame.[/p][p][/p][p]Not all enemies wear the same armor, you’ll encounter armor tiers ranging from steel to hardened steel to gold titanium alloy, which is both stronger and lighter than steel. That means not all of your bullets will have an easy time taking down all enemy types, because every caliber comes with realistic penetration values, so where you aim matters too. Light calibers, for example, will struggle against even basic armor, while the mid-to-heavy calibers can pierce hardened or titanium alloy. Shotguns also have different gauges with varying impact. But the elite officers will be wearing the best tier armor, so aim smart and prepare for a challenge.[/p][p][/p][p]Officers are designed to feel like cinematic mini-boss encounters. They’ve got complex AI, heavy loot, and unique abilities tailored to challenge you directly. It’s a sharp contrast between you mowing down troops of soldiers with your modern firepower (or vehicle).[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44889766/279952dc7fc1032d3757998af21bccd7e3b63fd4.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][h2][b]Behind the Scenes: Challenging Troop[/b][/h2][p][/p][p]One of the biggest challenges in our development when it came to units was the Cavalry. Balancing their AI (especially in multiplayer) was tough. While charging through crowds, horses have to also respond to being shot or losing a rider, and behave independently if dismounted.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44889766/11f3229ff35263f8432c9daf613d143bae6ba953.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][h2][b]Looking Ahead[/b][/h2][p][/p][p]There are so many things we want to add to Kingmakers; the possibilities feel endless, and that's exactly why we’re launching in Early Access first. [/p][p][/p][p] Post-Early Access, we want to add new factions such as the Scottish or French, have epic castle sieges, deeper troop officer systems, and maybe even a PvP mode. Helicopters and planes for you to pilot are also something we’d love to have and while that’s not unit-related, we could dive more into your arsenal and vehicles in a future dev blog! [/p][p]Mod support is in the works too and we can’t wait to see what creative chaos you will come up with it.

[/p][h2][b]Thanks for your support![/b][/h2][p][/p][p]That concludes our first Kingmakers dev blog! [/p][p][/p][p]We hope you enjoyed this deep dive into units and Kingmaker's strategy gameplay. We have so much more to share, so if you found this interesting, let us know what topic you want us to cover next in the comments, and we’ll post more of these on a regular as we get ready for early access [b]launch on October 8th[/b].[/p][p] [/p][p]Until then, [b][url="https://discord.gg/fTvDsAYDfU"]join the Discord[/url] [/b]and come hangout with us![/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][i]- The Kingmakers Team[/i][/p]

notes.title: Modern military medieval sandbox Kingmakers gets a release date this October
notes.content:
“The lyf so short, the craft so long to lerne," wrote Chaucer. But you'd trained hard with that crossbow, and let any man in bolting distance try to claim you hadn't mastered it. You never wanted to go to war, but the crops were failing, you'd just lost your seventeenth child to medium-pox, and dark portents swirled on the horizon like curdled goat's milk. Also, the actual goat's milk was curdling.

In that tent, you'd communed with angels, and the righteous fury of all the heavens coursed through every fibre of your being. You'd likely die today, you knew. But you'd die knowing you did all you could to put this fair kingdom to rights. You step outside, breathe deep the morning air, and immediately eat a point blank pump-action shotgun to the torso. Then you lose both your legs to the tank shell. Then someone runs over your corpse with a dirtbike. Bloody typical.

notes.title: Kingmakers: Early Access Release Date Announcement
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=52u8LIuzA-Y;full][/previewyoutube]

Dust off your rifles, mercenaries — [b]Kingmakers is officially entering Early Access on October 8th, 2025.[/b]

We know. Some of you were expecting it sooner, and we didn’t land in Q2. But building a game where time-traveling mercs drop air strikes on medieval knights takes a hell of a lot of toiling. We want to give you a game that hits hard and holds up, and the devs are grinding away to give you just that.

👉 [b][url=https://youtu.be/52u8LIuzA-Y]Watch the Release Date Reveal Trailer[/url] from the tinyBuild Connect Showcase[/b]
👉 [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2109770/Kingmakers/][b]Wishlist to be notified the second it drops [/b][/url]
👉 [b][url=https://discord.gg/fTvDsAYDfU]Join the Discord[/url] to chat with the devs, tune in to future FAQs, Q&As, and giveaways[/b]

notes.title: Kingmakers doesn't have a release date yet, but a movie is locked with Sonic production company Story Kitchen
notes.content:
Kingmakers, developed by Redemption Road and to be published by tinyBuild, recently took everyone by surprise with its eccentric (and technically impressive) first trailer, and while we don't have a release date yet, it seems that Hollywood is already interested in bringing it to the big screen.

Via GamesBeat, we've learned that Story Kitchen, a recently-formed production company behind the Sonic the Hedgehog movies and the upcoming Tomb Raider animated series (as well as many other gaming-related projects), has signed a deal to help develop a live-action movie based on the yet-to-be-released third-person shooter.

"The action, world-building, and intriguing sci-fi of Kingmakers make it a perfect concoction to build a propulsive new franchise in Hollywood... We have always been massive fans of tinyBuild. As publishers, they’re putting out great games that we love playing. We’ve kept a close eye on the things they’re working on and have been trying to figure out the next best opportunity to collaborate with them," said Story Kitchen cofounder Dmitri M. Johnson. Looking at Kingmakers' simple yet punchy premise, one can easily see how it could deftly translate will into an uncomplicated action movie that taps into several subgenres at once.

Read more

[b]We have partnered with Story Kitchen to bring you a live-action film adaptation[/b] of our upcoming medieval time-traveling action game that allows players to bring an arsenal of assault rifles, humvees, and attack helicopters to war-torn medieval England, where they’ll assist Owain Glyndower’s 1401 Welsh Rebellion, via massive simulated battles. Story Kitchen’s adaptation will ask the question: What if Braveheart included time travel?. 

We at tinyBuild and Redemption Road Games, will be working with Story Kitchen to develop the film, aiming to tell a unique story and establish the IP.

notes.title: Introducing Kingmakers
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=OvezgDni8z4;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3]Welcome soldier,[/h3]

We are thrilled to introduce you to Kingmakers, a solo or co-op action/strategy sandbox game with real-time simulated battles in a war-torn medieval era and a modern hero.  Prepare yourselves to build, lead, fight, and change the course of history!

We are Redemption Road Games, a passionate 20-person dev team that has dedicated over four years to crafting this immersive experience. Our focus has been on pioneering technology, pushing the boundaries of Unreal Engine to deliver an unparalleled gaming experience. From rendering and animations to sophisticated AI and cutting-edge online multiplayer code, we're confident that Kingmakers will stand out in the Unreal Engine landscape.

Drawing inspiration from beloved titles like the Mount and Blade series, Deeprock Galactic, Kingdom Come Deliverance, Chivalry, Stronghold series, World War Z, and so many more, we've curated a unique blend of inspirations to give you an epic experience.

We're planning to launch Kingmakers in Early Access on Steam later this year, and we'd like to invite you to join us on this incredible journey from the very beginning. When we open our gates to the community with Playtests, Demos and Early Access, we seek your invaluable input to shape the future of the game. Be part of the development process, and share your desires for what you wish to see in Kingmakers.

Your enthusiasm and support mean the world to us! Add Kingmakers to your Steam Wishlist, and connect with us on Discord or through our community channels linked below. Together, let's make history and forge an unforgettable legacy!
